newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Fresh political violence in Indonesia's Java.
newsitem.headline: Fresh political violence in Indonesia's Java.

text.p: Rioting by supporters of rival political parties erupted again on Indonesia's main Java island, and homes, offices and vehicles were damaged in at least two towns, police said on Thursday.
At least 14 people were injured in the violence on Wednesday, the Republika newspaper reported.
It was the latest in a series of violent incidents that have rocked Central Java province in the past two weeks.
The violence started after a popular folk singer switched political allegiance to the ruling Golkar party after campaigning in previous years for the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP).
The singer, Rhoma Irama, has announced he will be a Golkar candidate in the May 29 general elections, leading to much ire in PPP strongholds in central Java.

On Wednesday, PPP supporters clashed with Golkar cadres in the town of Wonosobo, 350 km (215 miles) east of Jakarta, the Republika said. It said 14 people were injured in the incident, but no arrests were made.
The newspaper said rioters damaged three government offices, 11 cars and dozens of houses.
Wonosobo police chief Lieutenant-Colonel Bambang Sutiarso said the town was calm on Thursday but declined to give further details.
But police in the neighbouring town of Banjarnegara said 10 PPP supporters were arrested after violence spread there.

"We have arrested 10 people after a clash on Wednesday. Five of them may be sent to court on charges of property damage and looting," Colonel Binarto, the police chief of Banyumas precinct, under which Banjaranegara falls, told Reuters.

"We don't know the motive behind their action. What we know is that they have attended a PPP function in Wonosobo," he said. "The clash occured when police tried to stop them from entering Banjaranegara. They damaged two police cars," he added.
Binarto added that a number of buildings were damaged in Banjaranegara.
Thirty people have brought to court and have been imprisoned for between three days and three months for their involvement in the violence two weeks ago.

Eight people were injured, at least 60 shops were burned or ransacked and a state-run bank was damaged during the violence in the town of Pekalongan, a coastal town some 300 km (190 miles) east of Jakarta.
